chunks: From him, from Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ayyūb al-Makkī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a Muslim woman praying while there is no head-covering upon her head.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as referring to young girls among women, excluding those who are mature, because it is not permissible for them to pray without a head-covering.

It is also possible that this was only permitted for them in a situation where they are unable to obtain anything with which to cover themselves; then it is permissible, in the circumstance as we have described, for them to pray without a head-covering.
And it is possible that what is meant by that is when she has upon herself a garment that covers her from her head to her feet, such as a wrap and the like.

As for the final report, it does not mention the free woman, and it is possible that this is specific to bondwomen, because it is permissible for a bondwoman to pray while there is no head-covering upon her. What we have previously presented of the reports indicates this, and clarifies it further.

key_terms.إِزَارٍ: a wrap-like garment covering the body
key_terms.الصِّغَرِ: young age; referring here to girls below maturity
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: reported narrations used as evidence in deriving the ruling
key_terms.الْبَالِغَاتِ: mature females who have reached legal adulthood
key_terms.الْحُرَّةِ: a free woman, as distinguished in legal rulings from a bondwoman
key_terms.قِنَاعٌ: a head-covering worn by a woman in the context of salat

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars interpret hadiths about a woman praying without a khimar or qina'?
ai.summary: This passage discusses how reports permitting a woman to pray without a head-covering are to be understood within fiqh. It explains that such reports may apply to young girls, cases of necessity, situations where a full-body garment already covers her, or to bondwomen rather than free women.
